questions.ask: What is your date of birth?
What is the postcode of the address we have on file for you?

intents.hardship: Financial hardship (job loss, illness, cannot cover essentials).
intents.dispute: "This isn't my debt" or "I never had that product".
intents.restructure: A request for a payment plan or lower instalments.
intents.too_much: The customer says the full amount is too much.

lines.opening: Hello, this is Isla, a digital assistant calling from Glenmorrow Savings Bank. We record this call.
lines.robot: Yes, I'm Isla, a digital assistant calling from Glenmorrow Savings Bank.
lines.scam: I understand your caution, and I will never ask for your PIN or passwords.
lines.purpose_before_verify: I can only explain that to {title} {last_name}, once I've confirmed who I'm speaking with.
lines.no_info: I'm sorry, I can't share any details about that.
lines.not_talk_once: I understand. This will only take a few minutes.
lines.tp_ask: When would be a good time to reach {title} {last_name}?
lines.tp_outside_window: I'm sorry, we can only call back between 9 am and 6:30 pm, today or on the next two business days. Is there another time that would work?
lines.tp_no_info: I'm sorry, I can only discuss this with {title} {last_name} personally.
lines.tp_booked: Thank you. We will call back on {date} at {time}.
lines.wrong_number: Thank you for letting me know, and sorry to have bothered you.
lines.condolence: I'm very sorry for your loss.
lines.id_intro: Before I go on, I need to ask you two security questions.
lines.id_why: We ask these questions to make sure we only speak with the right person and keep your information safe.
lines.id_explain: These questions protect you, because they make sure no one else can hear your private information.
lines.id_declined: I understand. Without these answers I can't go on with this call.
lines.id_repeat: Sorry, could you repeat that, please?
lines.id_wrong: I'm sorry, that doesn't match our records.
lines.id_failed: I'm sorry, I couldn't confirm your identity, so I can't go on with this call. Please visit a branch or use online banking.
lines.disclose_intro: Thank you, {first_name}. I'm calling about overdue payments on your account.
lines.product_line: Your {name} is {amount} in arrears, and {days} days overdue.
lines.ask_today: Can you pay the full {amount} today?
lines.ask_today_multi: Can you pay both in full today?
lines.offer_floor_date: I understand. Could you pay {amount} on {date}?
lines.below_floor: I'm sorry, I can't record less than {floor}. Could you pay {floor}?
lines.below_floor_again: I understand, but I can't accept less than the minimum amount.
lines.date_past: I'm sorry, that date has already passed. Could you choose a date from today onwards?
lines.not_business_day: That day isn't a business day. The next business day is {date}. Would that work?
lines.after_deadline: I'm sorry, the latest date I can accept is {date}. Could you pay by then?
lines.vague_ask: Which exact day would you pay?
lines.ask_date_for_amount: On which date would you pay {amount}?
lines.repeat_offer: Just to repeat, could you pay {amount} on {date}?
lines.readback_intro: Let me read back what we agreed.
lines.clamped_note: For your {name}, the latest date I can accept is {date}, so I've used that date.
lines.recorded: Thank you. Your promise has been recorded.
lines.record_failed: I'm sorry, your promise could not be recorded because of a system problem.
lines.paid_line: Thank you. Payments can take two business days to show on your account.
lines.dispute_line: I understand. I won't ask you for a payment on that product today.
lines.hardship: I'm very sorry to hear you're going through this. I'm passing you to our care team, who can help.
lines.restructure_line: I'll put you through to our arrears solutions team, who can talk to you about a payment plan.
lines.human_ask_help: I may be able to help you myself. Would you like to carry on with me?
lines.transfer: I'm transferring you now. Please hold.
lines.anything_else: Is there anything else I can help you with?
lines.promise_change: I'm sorry, I can't change a promise on this call.
lines.goodbye: Thank you for your time. Goodbye.
lines.confirm_again: Sorry, I didn't catch that. Do you confirm, yes or no?
lines.callback_failed: I'm sorry, I couldn't book the callback.
lines.transfer_failed: I'm sorry, the transfer didn't go through.
lines.system_error: I'm sorry, our system isn't responding right now.
lines.below_floor_final: I'm sorry, I can't record less than {amount}.

assumptions: The memo (19 Oct 2026) wins over policy v3.2 and over the old code list wherever they disagree, as the email and the memo both say.
Bands: memo A changes early to 1-14 and mid to 15-30. Late stays 31-60. Deadlines and attempts (1/2/3) are unchanged.
Holidays: the policy's bank holidays (2026-11-30, 2026-12-25, 2026-12-28, 2027-01-01, 2027-01-04) plus 2026-12-11 from memo B. 24 Dec 2026 is a normal business day.

The 'refused' code is retired (memo C). 'declined' is used as the close_call reason and the add_note reason for refusals. Rule 25's add_note reason 'refused' becomes 'declined', which matches the API enum.

Callback window changed to 09:00-18:30, both included (memo D). Days are today or one of the next two business days, shown as ['today','within_business_days:2']. business_days_only is true because calls only happen on business days and memo B bars callbacks on 11 Dec.
Callback: if the first time is outside the window, ask once more, so max_asks=2.
Confirm: close as unclear after a second unclear ask, so max_asks=2.

Identity: two wrong answers in total end the check (rule 9, which the memo keeps), so max_wrong=2. Date of birth is sent as DDMMYYYY (%d%m%Y). Postcode is sent in capitals with a space before the last 3 characters. No length is set for postcodes because their length varies.
date_order 'dmy' because the bank is in the UK and the system reads day first.
The verify_identity response has no hint field (its fields are ok, error, verified, wrong_answers_left, all_verified), so response.hint is empty and hints is empty.
Floor = 30% of arrears_amount, rounded up to a whole pound (floor_pct 30, floor_round up_unit). monthly_payment is never used. The memo confirms the floor is not lowered to 25%.
get_account amounts are in pounds and create_promise takes amount_pence, so promise_scale=100 and amount_scale=1.

Mid-band deadline: if it falls on a weekend or holiday it moves back to the previous business day (deadline_adjust previous_business_day). Late band: if today is already the last business day of the month, use the following month's last business day (roll_if_not_after_today).

Ladder step 2 is the full amount on the 5th business day after today, or the deadline if that is earlier. This is set as business_days_after:5 on the assumption that the engine caps any promise date at the product's deadline (rule 15).

Rule 21 (too much leads to the floor on the next step's date): step 2 is full_or_floor and step 3 is already the floor. The opening ask (full amount today) is attempt 1 (rules 16 and 20), so first_ask='today'.
Two products: a flat no to 'both in full today' counts as step 1 for each product (rule 23).
Hardship: rule 28 says to transfer to care_team with no offer and no notes on transfer. hardship_declined and hardship_short are only fallbacks. The hardship note is empty.
On any transfer no notes are written (rule 29), so transfer events carry no note.
The code list says 'refused' for no_ptp. The memo's 'declined' (also in the API enum) is used instead.
The payment-link text slide was dropped, so sms_line is empty.
The brief says nothing about 'next <weekday>' wording, so the default 'following_week' is used.
The brief says nothing about changing a recorded promise, so promise_change says it can't be changed on this call.
The brief says nothing about the 'I don't want to talk' limit, so max_not_talk keeps the default of 2.
after_promise.ask_anything_else and human.ask_first: rule 29 says to ask once before a human transfer. ask_anything_else keeps the default.
The brief says 'the call is recorded'. Following the spec's wording rule, the opening says 'We record this call.'
The brief does not name the floor in spoken words, so 'minimum amount' is used.
There are no extra call variables. All tool responses use the boolean 'ok' as their success flag.
